entities.description: Prior approaches were limited by an oversimplified aperture-flow/cooling treatment: the simple aperture-flow model neglected important physics such as fluid dynamics, particle charge effects, and particle mass loss from evaporation or droplet fission, while simple cooling could drive oscillation amplitudes too low for accurate frequency (and thus Q/M) measurements and often failed below about 1e-7 Torr because PLL tracking was lost.
entities.evidence_span: This model has obvious deficiencies: fluid dynamics and the effects of charge on the particles are neglected. Also, the complexities of mass loss of the particles as liquid evaporates or droplets fission are not considered.

evidence_spans: This model has obvious deficiencies: fluid dynamics and the effects of charge on the particles are neglected. Also, the complexities of mass loss of the particles as liquid evaporates or droplets fission are not considered.

However, measurements of trap oscillation frequencies (from which one can deduce Q/M) are best performed when the oscillation amplitudes are not too small. When this happens, the particle is not lost, but Q/M measurements are compromised.
